title: Irfan Pathan Backs CSK to Keep Rs 14.20 Crore Prashant Veer for IPL 2027
excerpt: Reports say Chennai Super Kings may release the 20-year-old all-rounder to free up funds after a quiet first season — but in a retain-or-release exercise for ESPNcricinfo, former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan kept Veer on the roster.
body:
• Cricbuzz reports Chennai Super Kings may release all-rounder Prashant Veer — bought for Rs 14.20 crore at the IPL 2026 auction — to free up funds, possibly to buy him back cheaper; a CSK official said no retention decision has been taken.
  • Veer, 20, scored 90 runs in six matches with no wickets in IPL 2026, with a highest score of 43 against Royal Challengers Bengaluru.
  • In an ESPNcricinfo retain-or-release exercise covering 23 players across the 10 franchises, Irfan Pathan retained 16 — including Veer — and released seven, among them Matheesha Pathirana and Trent Boult.
  • CSK's purse stands at Rs 2.4 crore, rising to Rs 7.4 crore with the annual salary-cap increment, ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction in Goa on December 16.

Chennai Super Kings have a Rs 14.20 crore question to answer before the IPL 2027 mini-auction, and Irfan Pathan thinks they should answer it by standing still. The former India all-rounder, making retain-or-release calls on 23 players across the 10 franchises for ESPNcricinfo, kept left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder Prashant Veer on CSK's roster — even as reports suggest the franchise is considering letting him go.

Why Veer is on the bubble

CSK bought Veer, then a teenager from Uttar Pradesh, for Rs 14.20 crore at the IPL 2026 auction in Abu Dhabi — one of two players the franchise signed at exactly that price. His first season did not match the fee: 90 runs in six matches across five innings, a highest score of 43 against Royal Challengers Bengaluru, and no wickets. Cricbuzz reported that CSK may release Veer to free up funds amid a perception that he "did not quite prove to be value for money," with a possible plan to buy him back at a lower price. A CSK official told Cricbuzz that no decision on retentions and releases has been taken.

"Cricbuzz reported that CSK may release Veer to free up funds amid a perception that he "did not quite prove to be value for money," with a possible plan to buy him back at a lower price."

The comparison inside CSK's own squad sharpens the dilemma. The other Rs 14.20 crore signing, 20-year-old wicketkeeper-batter Kartik Sharma of Rajasthan, scored 295 runs in 11 matches at an average of 32.77, with a highest score of 71 against Lucknow Super Giants — a season Cricbuzz says makes him the likelier of the two to be retained.

What Pathan would do

Pathan's exercise was unsentimental elsewhere: he released seven of the 23 players reviewed, including Rahul Chahar, Trent Boult, Matheesha Pathirana and Avesh Khan, while retaining 16 — Veer among them, alongside names such as Cameron Green, bought by Kolkata Knight Riders for Rs 25.20 crore, and Marcus Stoinis at Rs 11 crore. The logic of keeping Veer is the logic of his age and skill set: a 20-year-old left-arm spinner who bats is among the scarcest profiles in Indian T20 cricket, and one quiet season is a thin basis on which to sell low.

The money around the decision

CSK, five-time champions and now coached by Zaheer Khan, have Rs 2.4 crore of purse remaining, rising to Rs 7.4 crore with the annual Rs 5 crore salary-cap increment. Releasing Veer would add Rs 14.20 crore to that war chest — real money in a mini-auction — but would surrender a player the franchise valued at that price twelve months ago, with no guarantee of buying him back. Retention and release lists are due this month, ahead of the mini-auction in Goa on December 16 — described as the last mini-auction before the mega-auction that precedes the 2028 season. CSK's call on Veer will be one of its clearest tells.
